# playscape

> Beta Go library for where an agent's turn runs: sandboxed tools on bounded in-process pools of execution nodes, one shared workspace, and NGAC access control. A program composes it in code (`controlplane.NewMemory(inproc.NewFactory(registry, ws), recorder)`, then Deploy, Submit, SubmitAsync, Result); nothing in it listens on a port or reads configuration, and nothing is durable (retried runs belong to anchor). Access is defined in an NGAC policy machine (NIST-style users, attributes, associations, prohibitions; flat per-tool policies compile into the same graph) and enforced by the sandbox with default deny. The local workspace is confined to its directory with os.Root. Agents can spawn sub-agents through policy-gated self-reference. Tools of a run can execute in an isolated instance (`pkg/isolate`: Docker with runc or gVisor, no network, read-only root, non-root, limits), leased from a warm pool, one run per instance, never reused.

Go module `github.com/urmzd/playscape` (stdlib only). The Kubernetes Job runner is its own module, `github.com/urmzd/playscape/pkg/runner/k8s`. The `playscape` binary only validates a command in the sandbox: `playscape run [flags] COMMAND`.

- [README](README.md): features, installation, quick start, validating a command, limitations
- [Architecture overview](docs/architecture/overview.md): package DAG, pools, sandbox model, workspace confinement, the CLI, roadmap

## Examples

- [Basic](examples/basic/main.go): deploy, size the pool, submit, observe with a sandboxed tool
- [NGAC](examples/ngac/main.go): access as a policy graph with attribute grants, prohibitions, and spawn objects
- [Saige agents](examples/saige/main.go): AI agents as workloads, including agent-spawns-agent
